All three solutions give 4π, which is the total arc length of the whole curve rather than the perimeter of the region it encloses.

**Speed.** f'(θ) = i e^{iθ}(1+e^{iθ})², so |f'(θ)| = |1+e^{iθ}|² = 2 + 2cosθ. The total arc length over [0, 2π] is therefore 4π.

**Self-intersection.** Write u = 1 + e^{iθ}. Then f = (u³ − 1)/3, so two parameters give the same point exactly when their u³ values agree, i.e. u₂ = ωu₁ for a cube root of unity ω.

The circle |u − 1| = 1 meets its 120° rotation at u = 0 and at u = e^{±iπ/3}. This gives a crossing at f = −2/3, where u³ = −1, from the two parameter values θ = ±2π/3.

**Loop.** The part of the curve with θ between 2π/3 and 4π/3 is a small loop. It runs through the cusp at u = 0, where f = −1/3, and has |u³| < 1. This loop lies inside the larger outer arc, so it is not part of the boundary of R.

**Outer boundary.** The outer boundary is the arc with θ ∈ (−2π/3, 2π/3). Its length is
∫ 2(1+cosθ) dθ = 2[θ + sinθ] from −2π/3 to 2π/3 = 2(4π/3 + √3) = 8π/3 + 2√3.

This is about 11.84, not 4π ≈ 12.57. Solution 1 checked winding numbers only about w = 0 and missed the self-crossing.

All three solutions are incorrect. Solutions 2 and 3 also give final answers (3 and 4) that do not even match their own derived value of 4π.

VERDICT 1: REJECT
VERDICT 2: REJECT
VERDICT 3: REJECT
